q-137105.name: Question 1
q-137105.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

 

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $9a+\frac{b}{c}?$
q-137105.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 16 & -8 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}72 & -36 \\ -36 & 18\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}72 & -36 & 20 \\ -36 & 18 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}72 & -36 & 20 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{5}{18}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{18}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{18} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
9a+\frac{b}{c}=9\cdot \frac{5}{18}+\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{1}=3.
$$

A=[−214−2−21],b=[31−5],W=[100020001]

Consider the matrices A and W, and the vector b shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem WAx=Wb is [a0]+x2[bc],x2∈R, what is the value of 9a+bc?

a
−2
b

Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the normal equation corresponding to WAx=Wb, we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by (WA)T:

(WA)T⋅WAx=(WA)T⋅WbAT(WTW)Ax=AT(WTW)b

Now, since

WTW=[120002200012]=[100040001],

our normal equation can be written, as follows:

[−24−21−21][100040001][−214−2−21][x1x2]=[−24−21−21][100040001][31−5][−24−21−21][−2116−8−21][x1x2]=[−24−21−21][34−5][72−36−3618][x1x2]=[20−10]

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[72−3620−3618−10]R2:=R2+12R1∼[72−3620000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we have x1=518+12x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[518+12x2x2]=[5180]+x2[121],x2∈R.

Therefore, we have

9a+bc=9⋅518+(12)1=3.

q-137878.name: Question 2
q-137878.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 20 \\ 20 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 29\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
q-137878.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {3}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 \\ -18 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -27\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}37 & 20 \\ 20 & 17\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}55 \\ 29\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=37+17+55=109.
$$

q-137886.name: Question 3
q-137886.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 20 \\ 20 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
q-137886.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 20 \\ 20 & 40\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=10+40+6=56.
$$

q-137924.name: Question 4
q-137924.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
q-137924.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -8 & 16 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -12 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}18 & -36 \\ -36 & 72\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}27 \\ -54\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -36 & 27 \\ -36 & 72 & -54\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}18 & -36 & 27 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{3}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=2\cdot \frac{3}{2}+\frac{2}{1}=5.
$$

q-137924.html:
Question 4
?

A=[1−2−241−2],b=[2−31],W=[100020001].

Consider the matrices A and W, and the vector b shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem WAx=Wb is [a0]+x2[bc],x2∈R, what is the value of 2a+bc?

a
3
b
6
c
7
d
8
e
5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To get the normal equation corresponding to WAx=Wb, we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by (WA)T:

(WA)T⋅WAx=(WA)T⋅WbAT(WTW)Ax=AT(WTW)b

Now, since

WTW=[120002200012]=[100040001],

our normal equation can be written as follows:

[1−21−24−2][100040001][1−2−241−2][x1x2]=[1−21−24−2][100040001][2−31][1−21−24−2][1−2−8161−2][x1x2]=[1−21−24−2][2−121][18−36−3672][x1x2]=[27−54]

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[18−3627−3672−54]R2:=R2+2R1∼[18−3627000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we have x1=32+2x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[32+2x2x2]=[320]+x2[21],x2∈R.

Therefore, we have

a+bc=2⋅32+21=5.

q-158373.name: Question 5
q-158373.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-158373.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {3}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 9 & -9 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}22 & -8 \\ -8 & 11\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}11 & 8 \\ 8 & 22\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{11\cdot 22-8\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}11 & 8 \\ 8 & 22\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{178}[\begin{aligned}178 \\ 178\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
